cards.title: Beyond Compliance: Understanding Modern Government Expectations
cards.description: Explore why cybersecurity is no longer just an IT function but a core measure of organizational reliability in defense contracting.

cards.title: SPRS: The Supplier Performance Risk System
cards.description: Understand how the Department of Defense uses SPRS to evaluate supplier reliability, predict risk and influence contract awards.

cards.title: Operational Maturity and Governance
cards.description: Move beyond documentation to build mature cybersecurity governance programs that survive scrutiny and demonstrate lasting operational discipline.

cards.title: Evidence Discipline and Operational Evidence
cards.description: Build evidence management systems that demonstrate control implementation and survive scrutiny during assessments and investigations.

cards.title: Corrective Actions as Operational Signals
cards.description: Use corrective action discipline as a competitive advantage to demonstrate organizational learning and improvement.

cards.title: Supplier Risk as an Acquisition Problem
cards.description: Understand why government views cybersecurity weaknesses as acquisition risks that affect mission assurance, delivery reliability, and contract performance.

cards.title: Integrity and Representation Risk
cards.description: Ensure your cybersecurity representations are defensible operationally and understand integrity considerations in government evaluation.

cards.title: Leadership Accountability in Cybersecurity Governance
cards.description: Build executive involvement and accountability structures that demonstrate organizational commitment to cybersecurity maturity.

cards.title: Building Integrated Governance Ecosystems
cards.description: Create aligned systems that integrate policies, procedures, evidence, technical implementation, training, and executive oversight.

cards.title: System Security Plan Development
cards.description: Develop honest, defensible SSPs that accurately describe your operational implementations and survive scrutiny.

cards.title: Cybersecurity Programs That Survive Operational Stress
cards.description: Design governance programs that remain defensible and functional during incidents, disputes, and investigations.

cards.title: Governance and Organizational Trust
cards.description: Build stronger long-term credibility within government contracting by making cybersecurity governance a trust indicator

cards.title: Audit and Accountability
cards.subtitle: Track system activities for security compliance
items: Define audit events requiring logging
Create, protect, and retain system audit logs
Review and analyze system audit logs
Alert on audit logging process failures
Correlate audit logging information across systems
Protect audit information and tools
Limit access to audit functionality
Time-stamp audit records using synchronized clocks
Automate audit record analysis

cards.title: Awareness and Training
cards.subtitle: Educate users and staff on security practices
items: Provide security awareness training
Provide role-based security training
Update training on organizational information security incidents

cards.title: Configuration Management
cards.subtitle: Manage and control system configurations
items: Establish and maintain information system baseline configurations
Establish and enforce security configuration settings
Monitor system components and information for unauthorized changes
Monitor information system security
Restrict, disable, or prevent nonessential programs
Apply security settings to IT products
Track and document configuration changes
Analyze security impacts of proposed changes
Control physical and logical access to configuration

cards.title: Identification and Authentication
cards.subtitle: Uniquely identify and authenticate users and devices
items: Identify system users, processes, or devices
Authenticate (or verify) the identity of users, processes, or devices
Use multifactor authentication for network access
Employ replay-resistant authentication mechanisms
Store and transmit passwords securely
Enforce password complexity and expiration
Disable accounts after specified inactivity periods
Lock out accounts after consecutive failed attempts
Prevent password reuse across cycles
Obscure password entry fields during typing
Use certificate-based authentication where applicable

cards.title: Access Control
cards.subtitle: Limit system access to authorized users and processes
items: Limit system access to authorized users
Limit system access to the types of transactions and functions
Control the flow of CUI in accordance with approved authorizations
Separate the duties of individuals to reduce risk of malevolent activity
Employ the principle of least privilege
Use non-privileged accounts when accessing non-security functions
Prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions
Limit unsuccessful logon attempts
Provide privacy and security notices before granting access
Use session lock with pattern-hiding screensavers
Terminate sessions automatically after defined conditions
Monitor and control remote access sessions
Employ cryptographic mechanisms to protect confidentiality of remote access
Route remote access through managed access control points
Authorize wireless access prior to allowing connection
Protect wireless access using authentication and encryption
Control connection of mobile devices to organizational systems
Encrypt CUI on mobile computing devices
Verify and control connection to external systems
Control information posted or processed on publicly accessible systems
Limit use of portable storage devices on external systems
Control execution of embedded software code

cards.title: Media Protection
cards.subtitle: Protect physical and digital media containing CUI
items: Protect system media containing CUI (paper and digital)
Limit access to CUI on system media to authorized users
Sanitize or destroy system media prior to disposal or reuse
Mark media with necessary CUI markings
Control access to media containing CUI during transportation
Maintain accountability for system media during transportation
Protect backups containing CUI at storage locations
Restrict the use of portable storage devices
Prohibit use of portable storage devices when unauthorized

cards.title: Physical Protection
cards.subtitle: Protect physical facility and system infrastructure
items: Limit physical access to organizational systems and equipment
Protect and monitor physical facility perimeter
Escort visitors and monitor visitor activity
Maintain audit logs of physical access
Control and manage physical access devices
Enforce physical security for organizational assets

cards.title: System and Information Integrity
cards.subtitle: Identify, report, and correct system flaws promptly
items: Identify, report, and correct system flaws in a timely manner
Provide protection against malicious code at appropriate locations
Monitor system security alerts and advisories
Update malicious code protection mechanisms when available
Perform periodic scans of the system and real-time scans of files
Monitor system for unauthorized communications
Identify unauthorized use of organizational systems
